title: The experiment pilot can run only once, cannot extend enrollment, and can lose or rewrite its own result
detail:
Found reading the pilot code for LIVE-2281; no pilot has run, so nothing is lost yet. CONFIRMED in source: (1) analytics_experiment_manage has no path out of completed and the key is unique, so the one catalog pilot can be run once ever; an inconclusive run on thin traffic spends it. (2) Assignment stops at started_at + minimum_days and pause does not stop that clock, so a slow week cannot be extended. (3) finish stamps guardrails_reviewed_at = now() at enrollment close, before the 7-day follow-up the review is supposed to cover exists. (4) The 180-day retention purge deletes assignments, which fires the exclusion trigger, so a completed result can later read as inconclusive (lib/analytics/experiments.ts). LIKELY, not yet proven: (5) recordConfirmedRsvp is called un-awaited from app/(main)/events/actions.ts and the outcome path then reads cookies() in lib/analytics/experiment-runtime.ts, which can fail silently once the response is sent, losing the outcome. (6) lib/analytics/rsvp-telemetry.ts skips the outcome when the idempotent event.rsvp row already exists, so a member who RSVPed before exposure never converts. WHY IT MATTERS: the first real pilot after launch would produce a result nobody can trust or repeat. FIX DIRECTION: an additive migration that lets a completed key be re-drafted as a new run (run number in the seed), stops the clock while paused, records the guardrail review as its own later command, and snapshots arm totals at completion so the purge cannot change them; await the outcome write inside the request (after()) and count a first post-exposure RSVP. Fix before LIVE-2281 starts a pilot.

2026-11-16 code-only pass (no migration, no production write, no pilot started). FIXED, point 5: the RSVP action now hands the confirmed-RSVP telemetry to after() through scheduleConfirmedRsvp (lib/analytics/rsvp-telemetry.ts), so the event.rsvp ledger write and the experiment outcome finish inside the request, where cookies() is still readable, and the RSVP is not delayed. Outside a request scope it falls back to the old best-effort write and logs a warning. Unit test: lib/analytics/rsvp-telemetry.schedule.test.ts (the promise after() holds settles only once the outcome write has). NOT FIXED, point 6: lib/analytics/rsvp-telemetry.test.ts pins the current behaviour ('does not count a duplicate or rejected ledger write as an experiment outcome'), and track() returns one boolean for both duplicate and rejected, so counting a post-exposure RSVP needs an owner call on that test and a way to tell the two apart. Its reach is narrower than filed: the idempotency key is per (event, member), so an RSVP to a different event after exposure does convert; only a withdraw and re-RSVP to an event the member already RSVPed to before exposure is skipped. NOT FIXED, points 1 to 4: all four live in the SQL functions and trigger of migration 20270346050000 (analytics_experiment_manage, the assign and outcome windows, guardrails_reviewed_at in finish, the purge and exclusion trigger) and need the additive migration plus pgTAP tests the probe names. Row stays open.

2026-11-17 SQL pass (additive migration 20270346084000_analytics_experiment_runs.sql; not applied to any database, no pilot started). FIXED, points 1 to 4. (1) Each pilot run is its own row with a run number: the key is unique per (key, run), at most one run of a key is open, and draft on a completed run whose guardrail review is recorded inserts run N+1 with its own ID, so its assignment seed, assignments and outcomes are separate; the earlier run's row and result stay as history. (2) A pause that begins inside the enrollment window sets paused_at; resuming adds the paused time to paused_for, and the assign, expose and outcome windows and the finish check all use started_at + minimum_days + paused_for, so a paused pilot keeps its remaining days (finish is refused while paused inside the window). (3) finish only closes enrollment. review_guardrails is its own command, refused until finished_at + conversion_days. The admin panel now closes enrollment, then records the review, then offers a new run. (4) Per-arm totals are frozen into results_snapshot once follow-up is over: at the review, or by analytics_experiment_purge before it deletes anything. analytics_experiment_results reads the snapshot for a frozen run, so a later purge or consent withdrawal cannot change it. Residual: a membership aged past 180 days while its run is still enrolling or in follow-up (only possible after long pauses) is still purged and counted as an exclusion, which reads inconclusive, as intended for data lost before the result is final. Proof: supabase/tests/analytics_experiment_runs.test.sql (21 assertions; run here against a local PostgreSQL 16 with both experiment migrations and a minimal pgTAP shim, 21 of 21 and the existing analytics_experiments.test.sql 17 of 17; db-tests runs the real pgTAP in CI). Point 5 stays fixed (lib/analytics/rsvp-telemetry.schedule.test.ts). NOT FIXED, point 6, outside this row's pass condition: lib/analytics/rsvp-telemetry.test.ts still pins the skip of a duplicate ledger write as an outcome; it needs an owner call and a way to tell a duplicate from a rejected write.

verify.note: Measures the four SQL consequences at their sources: the pgTAP file holds the re-run, kept-enrollment-days, review-after-follow-up (and refused before) and purge-proof-result assertions; in the replayed migrations the newest analytics_experiment_manage finish branch no longer stamps the guardrail review and a review_guardrails command exists; the newest assign window counts paused_for; results and purge read and write results_snapshot; and the point 5 unit test exists. Fails on the tree before this change at the first arm. Cannot see whether the migration is applied (check:migrations owns that) or the pgTAP verdict itself (db-tests owns that).
